item.title: May 26th, 2026
item.author: xxxx
item.description:
Very excited to promote our most recent paper where we use our PLIP+Q MLIP to study growth mechanisms in ZnO nanoparticle following atom by atom deposition. We show that (1) our simple approach for long-range interactions remains reliable for such complex simulation and (2) growth can induce phase transition from a metastable state.

Kudos to all of the participants of this exciting work: Quentin Gromoff, Carlos R. Salazar, Magali BENOIT and Jacek Goniakowski

item.title: January 7th, 2026
item.author: xxxx
item.description: Can a system as thoroughly studied as the Lennard-Jones gas still reveal intriguing phenomena? In a collaboration with the Laboratoire de Physique de la Matière Condensée published in Phys Rev Letters, we employed Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations and rare-event sampling to investigate liquid nucleation from the vapor phase. Contrary to the predictions of Classical Nucleation Theory, our results demonstrate that critical clusters nucleate at a density significantly different from that of the macroscopic equilibrium liquid. We rationalize these numerical findings using a two-variable nucleation theory that is both accessible and highly effective.

item.title: September 26th, 2025
item.author: xxxx
item.description: Very excited to announce that our projet NanoPHIA is now funded by the PEPR Diadem! We will receive 905k€ to work on the formation process in physical synthesis of nanoparticles by exploiting AI to couple characterisation, in-situ measurement and simulations. It will a collaboration with CEMES, INSP and ILM and 4 postdocs will be hired soon to do both simulations and experiments.
